multi_column.title: Multi-column layout / gutter detection
multi_column.summary: text lines merged across column boundaries, or column order inverted (right column read before left)
multi_column.note: assemble::assemble_reading_order's XY-cut now qualifies a vertical gutter against the page's own median character size (MIN_GUTTER_EMS), not just a fixed page-width fraction (MIN_CUT_FRACTION), so narrow (1 em) column gutters recover column-major order the same way wide ones already did

footnote.title: Footnotes
footnote.summary: footnote text merged into body `Text` region instead of classified as `Footnote`; footnote markers (superscript numerals) not linked to their note
footnote.note: classified via layout::classify_block's footnote rule (requires a block to sit low on the page, carry a smaller font than the rest of the page, and open with a recognized footnote marker). serialize::render_block now has a Footnote arm too (`[^marker]: text`, marker taken from the block's own leading digit/symbol) -- marker-to-note *linking* (resolving a superscript reference elsewhere in the body back to its note) is still open.

header_footer.title: Page headers/footers repeated across pages
header_footer.summary: header/footer text leaking into the body text stream; running headers misclassified as `Section-header`
header_footer.note: layout::band_of's shape test (thin strip, detached from the body by a minimum gap) plus a cross-page repeated_running_bands pass, suppressed in serialize::render_block

multi_line_table_cell.title: Nested/multi-line table cells
multi_line_table_cell.summary: cells spanning multiple visual lines merged incorrectly with adjacent rows; rowspan/colspan not detected

blocked.reason: This pitfall's PDF-backed corpus case fails one step upstream of classification: real Stage 1 block grouping (extract::group_chars_into_blocks) already merges the row's cells together across the column gap into one block, so no separate per-cell block exists left for graphics::table_grid_cells to assign to a grid cell. graphics.rs (Stage 1b) now detects the table and reconstructs its grid from ruling lines correctly wherever cells survive as distinct blocks -- see merged_table_cell and figure_caption, unblocked by the same code path -- but this case's problem is upstream of that.
blocked.unblocked_by: Teach extract::group_chars_into_blocks to stop a line/block merge at a ruling line boundary from Page::graphics, instead of only using vertical-gap/x-gap heuristics blind to the table grid.

multi_line_table_cell.pdf_backed_reason: Real Stage 1 block grouping merges the row's cells together across the column gap in a way a hand-authored already-split `Document` can't demonstrate.

merged_table_cell.title: Merged table cells (rowspan/colspan)
merged_table_cell.summary: TEDS-Struct penalizes tree-topology mismatches here most heavily
merged_table_cell.note: graphics::detect_table_regions + graphics::table_grid_cells (Stage 1b) now detect a bordered table from its ruling lines and assign a block spanning multiple grid cells to every cell it overlaps, resolving a merged/rowspan cell correctly -- see the corpus cases now carrying synthetic `graphics` ruling-line fixtures.

borderless_table.title: Borderless / whitespace-delimited tables
borderless_table.summary: no ruling lines for the layout model to key off; frequently misclassified as plain `Text`
borderless_table.note: Closed by layout::whitespace_column_corridors — a shared-whitespace-corridor heuristic over a single block's lines, complementing detect_borderless_table_regions's side-by-side-blocks shape.

nested_formula.title: Nested mathematical formulas
nested_formula.summary: inline formulas embedded mid-sentence not separated from surrounding text; multi-line/stacked formulas (fractions, summations, matrices) fragmented into multiple bounding boxes
nested_formula.note: Display (block-level) formulas are now classified via layout::is_display_formula -- a geometric-plus-lexical heuristic requiring a block to be centered, narrow relative to the page, vertically isolated from its neighbours by roughly a line height, dense with math symbols/digits, and not end like a sentence. Both seeded cases (an isolated display formula and a two-line stacked fraction) now pass. *Inline* formulas embedded mid-sentence in a body paragraph are still open -- see blocked below.

blocked.reason: An inline formula shares its block with ordinary prose, so there is no separate bounding box or whitespace/isolation signal for a geometric heuristic to key off the way there is for a display formula -- distinguishing 'e=mc^2' embedded mid-sentence from surrounding text needs actual layout/vision understanding, not just geometry.
blocked.unblocked_by: Stage 4b vision detector -- inline formula segmentation is the one sub-case in this registry that still needs it.

super_subscript.title: Superscript/subscript handling
super_subscript.summary: footnote markers, exponents, and chemical/math subscripts causing baseline-clustering errors in Stage 1's line grouping
super_subscript.note: extract::group_words's is_script_continuation check now recognizes a smaller, baseline-offset, nearby character as a super/subscript of its predecessor and attaches it to its base instead of splitting it off
super_subscript.pdf_backed_reason: A character-extraction/baseline-clustering failure in the real PDFium text layer; a synthetic already-grouped `Document` gives Stage 1's baseline clustering nothing to get wrong. **Fixed** — this is the one PDF-backed case that already passes the scoreboard.

rotated_text.title: Rotated or vertical text
rotated_text.summary: sidebar labels, rotated table headers, CJK vertical text (relevant given Traditional Chinese/Japanese document support)
rotated_text.note: Handles 90-degree-rotated Latin runs (sidebar labels) via extract::merge_rotated_text_runs. Char::angle_degrees now also carries PDFium's own reported glyph rotation directly (extract::extract_char), rather than only the geometric run-inference merge_rotated_text_runs falls back to when it's unavailable. CJK vertical writing mode is still unhandled.
rotated_text.pdf_backed_reason: Needs real glyph rotation data from PDFium's text layer.

figure_caption.title: Figure/caption association
figure_caption.summary: captions not correctly linked to their parent `Picture`/`Table` region, or associated with the wrong figure when multiple figures share a page
figure_caption.note: layout::is_caption covers the caption half. graphics::detect_picture_regions (Stage 1b) now emits RegionClass::Picture from Image/XObjectForm page objects (plus large text-free Fill graphics) -- see the corpus cases now carrying synthetic `graphics` image fixtures. Associating a caption with the *correct* Picture when multiple figures share a page (nearest-neighbor matching) is still open.

list_nesting.title: List-item nesting
list_nesting.summary: multi-level bullet/numbered lists collapsed into flat `List-item` blocks, losing hierarchy
list_nesting.note: reading order now passes after the narrow-gutter fix shared with multi-column above -- each side-by-side outline is read fully before the next; hierarchy/depth itself is still not modeled, so nested lists still flatten into one flat sequence

cross_page_continuation.title: Cross-page table/paragraph continuation
cross_page_continuation.summary: tables or paragraphs split across a page boundary not stitched back together
cross_page_continuation.pdf_backed_reason: Needs a real multi-page extraction; `assemble_reading_order` only operates within a single page, and a synthetic multi-page `Document` wouldn't exercise the actual stitching gap PDFium extraction produces.

section_header_vs_bold.title: Section headers vs. bold body text
section_header_vs_bold.summary: `Section-header` misclassified as `Title` or emphasized `Text` when font-weight is the only visual cue
section_header_vs_bold.note: Char::font_weight now carries PDFium's own reported font weight (extract::extract_char, via PdfPageTextChar::font_weight) alongside the existing font-*name* heuristic (layout::is_bold_font_name). The classifier itself does not yet threshold on the numeric weight -- see unblocked_by.

blocked.reason: layout::classify_block's bold-heading signal still only reads the font *name* (is_bold_font_name), not the new Char::font_weight field -- the signal now exists in the data model but classify_block hasn't been updated to prefer it over the name heuristic.
blocked.unblocked_by: Thread a block's median Char::font_weight into classify_block and prefer it over is_bold_font_name when present (a font that declares its weight numerically is a stronger signal than a name-string guess).

embedded_font.title: Embedded/CID-keyed fonts and ligatures
embedded_font.summary: pdfium character extraction dropping or garbling glyphs from non-standard font encodings

blocked.reason: pdfium-render 0.9.3 (and PDFium's FPDF_TEXTPAGE API) expose no raw charcode, /Encoding, or /Differences accessor, so Stage 1 cannot re-resolve glyph-name-derived Unicode against the base encoding. Separately, the corpus case's `page` is a frozen extract_baseline snapshot, so an extract.rs fix cannot move the scoreboard until examples/stage3_pdf_cases.rs regenerates it. Note this is a narrower gap than it first appears: PDFium resolves ToUnicode internally for the common case, so this is specifically about non-standard/custom /Differences encodings PDFium's own resolution doesn't cover -- not a general 'PDFium can't read fonts' problem.
blocked.unblocked_by: A charcode-level PDF reader independent of PDFium -- e.g. `lopdf` (xref + FlateDecode + content-stream tokenizing) paired with an Adobe Glyph List table, walking each page's /Font resource dict's /Encoding /Differences to re-resolve glyph names the way firecrawl/pdf-inspector does on the same lopdf substrate -- or an upstream pdfium-render API exposing per-char charcodes; then regenerate the PDF-backed snapshot.

embedded_font.pdf_backed_reason: Needs a real custom-encoded/CID-keyed font to reproduce dropped/garbled glyphs.

overlapping_text.title: Overlapping/z-ordered text objects
overlapping_text.summary: watermarks, stamps, or redaction boxes overlapping real text and corrupting bbox clustering

blocked.reason: Page::graphics now carries a real page-object paint-order z-index (extract::extract_graphics), and Char::fill_color now carries each character's own fill color -- both signals this pitfall needs are now in the data model. Nothing yet reads them to resolve an overlap (e.g. drop a low-z, faint-fill-colored watermark run before it corrupts bbox clustering).
blocked.unblocked_by: In extract.rs or layout.rs, use Char::fill_color (a very light gray/faint fill is a watermark signal) and relative z-order between overlapping text runs to suppress or de-prioritize the watermark run before block clustering.

overlapping_text.pdf_backed_reason: Needs real z-ordered text objects from a PDF.
